edits.match: The nasal valve regulates the rate of airflow and the slight resistance it provides helps to keep the lungs expanded.
edits.replacement: The nasal valve regulates the rate of airflow and is the site of greatest resistance in the nasal airway.
edits.reason: UNSUPPORTED: 'helps to keep the lungs expanded' is not in the cited StatPearls Nose chapter; the retrieved excerpt supports only that the valve is the flow-limiting, highest-resistance segment.

notes: SUPPORTED: nasal valve borders (upper lateral cartilage, septum, head of inferior turbinate) and flow-limiting role; turbinate mucosa swelling regulating resistance; olfactory epithelium at roof/upper septum; anterior septum (Kiesselbach/Little's area) as commonest bleeding site. GENERAL KNOWLEDGE (correct): nasal bones articulating with frontal bone and maxillae, upper lateral and major alar cartilages, vomer in septum, meatuses receiving sinus and nasolacrimal drainage, trigeminal sensation, internal/external carotid supply, conducting-zone function. Clinical text consistent with NHS trust leaflets (not retrieved). Structures valid; references https on approved hosts.
